incidents.victim: Node.js, Python, and other software using the Brotli compression library
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decompression library (CVE-2026-111497), triggered by sending malicious compressed data to any application that decompresses Brotli content.
incidents.impact: The flaw enables remote code execution across a broad swath of the software ecosystem, including Node.js, Python Brotli bindings, the Bun runtime, and the Envoy and Istio proxies; patches are rolling out across dozens of downstream projects.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised customer accounts and stole AI API keys as part of a broader, industry-wide campaign against AI infrastructure providers.
incidents.impact: Stolen API keys and infrastructure access are being resold on underground forums, letting other actors run workloads on victims' accounts and bills.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached an internal CRM platform used by business partners to sell energy contracts.
incidents.impact: ENGIE is notifying customers of its French gas supply business about the breach; the scope of data exposure is still being assessed.

incidents.vector: A threat actor used a master key leaked in May 2026 from the experimental LiteLLM Agent Platform to add an infostealer to a released LiteLLM version.
incidents.impact: Users who installed the affected release were exposed to an embedded infostealer before the compromised version was identified and pulled.

incidents.vector: An intruder gained access to internal business systems through a learning management system and a CRM platform.
incidents.impact: Internal business systems were accessed; Genesys says it found no evidence the intruder pivoted to its public customer-facing cloud environments.

incidents.vector: An infinite-mint smart-contract exploit allowed attackers to create tokens without authorization.
incidents.impact: Attackers minted and stole approximately $2.7 million worth of tokens from the Initia project.

incidents.victim: Small number of Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) staff devices
incidents.vector: Malicious ads served by an Israeli ad-tech company delivered zero-click spyware to staff devices.
incidents.impact: ABC wiped the affected devices as a precaution; the broadcaster says it found no confirmed evidence of compromise.

incidents.vector: A flaw in eMudhra's April 2025 key-generation ceremony produced a second set of weak private keys for eight intermediate CA certificates, cutting their effective entropy to single/double-digit bits.
incidents.impact: The weak keys could let an attacker derive private keys, forge trusted TLS or code-signing certificates, and impersonate websites or services; browser vendors have blocked the affected keys and eMudhra has revoked the certificates.

incidents.victim: Websites and applications running PHP worldwide
incidents.vector: Two unauthenticated remote-code-execution vulnerabilities in PHP core (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619), dubbed PHP2Shell, are triggerable via a single crafted HTTP request and affect every PHP version since 5.4.
incidents.impact: An estimated 70%+ of websites run PHP, with tens of millions of exposed instances cited by CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks; CISA, NSA and the FBI issued urgent patching advisories, and SANS reports targeted exploitation underway even though a fully reliable universal exploit has not yet emerged.

incidents.victim: 600+ organizations across the Americas, Europe, and Australia, including Conduent and Microlise
incidents.vector: SafePay actors gain access via compromised credentials and exploitation of known vulnerabilities in internet-facing VPN and remote-access devices, then use legitimate IT tools to move laterally and disable backups before exfiltrating and encrypting data.
incidents.impact: CISA and the FBI call SafePay one of the most active ransomware groups of 2026; past victim Conduent, a government technology contractor, reached an $80 million class-action settlement tied to a prior SafePay attack that disrupted Medicaid, child support, and toll services.

incidents.victim: Hundreds of ConnectWise Cloud Backup customers (~1,000 Microsoft 365 tenants affected)
incidents.vector: A threat actor obtained a sensitive API secret for ConnectWise's Cloud Backup application, letting them request access tokens into any customer Microsoft 365 tenant where the app was installed without any action by the customer.
incidents.impact: Huntress confirmed unauthorized sign-ins across 162 tenants and successful logins in more than 300 of nearly 1,000 Entra tenants; attackers performed Microsoft Graph API reconnaissance and added credentials to maintain backdoor access.

incidents.victim: Organizations across education, financial services, healthcare, government, manufacturing, and other sectors
incidents.vector: Multiple ransomware groups, including Qilin, Inc, and actors using Settra ransomware, exploit the May 2026 PAN-OS authentication bypass (CVE-2026-0257) to establish VPN sessions, then pivot to vCenter and ESXi hypervisors to dump domain controller credentials offline.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 has tracked exploitation since early June 2026 across numerous industries; attackers bypass MFA and endpoint detection by moving directly to the virtualization layer before deploying ransomware.

incidents.victim: A small number of BeyondTrust Remote Support customers
incidents.vector: Armory Castle (formerly tracked as UNC5221) exploited a zero-day file-upload vulnerability (CVE-2026-102764) in BeyondTrust Remote Support, then used a custom webshell and SUID-bit privilege escalation to gain root access and harvest credentials from the appliance's secrets vault.
incidents.impact: The group established root-level persistence that survives reboots, pivoted to the BeyondTrust admin console for lateral movement, and exfiltrated internal documents; Mandiant warns of potential broader opportunistic exploitation now that the flaw is public.

incidents.victim: A limited number of Ivanti Connect Secure customers
incidents.vector: Threat actor UTA0576 chained three zero-day vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-104935, in Ivanti Connect Secure to bypass authentication, execute code remotely, and escalate privileges on fully patched VPN appliances.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole credentials stored on the device, dumped Active Directory metadata, and conducted network reconnaissance; Ivanti fixed the remote-code-execution component but is still developing a fix for the remaining vulnerability in the exploit chain.

incidents.vector: An opportunistic attacker used compromised credentials obtained through a third-party-managed external gateway appliance with weak authentication enforcement to access internal systems, then conducted months of noisy network scanning, brute-force login attempts, and internal document scraping.
incidents.impact: The intrusion was contained after Cortex XDR blocked an attempt to exploit a WSUS remote-code-execution vulnerability on the bank's central configuration management server; Unit 42 found no persistent backdoors and the bank rotated all exposed credentials.
